lessons.title: Start with three forms you know
lessons.gloss: return to three familiar possessive bases before agreement forms

segments.text: Say ਮੇਰਾ, ਤੁਹਾਡਾ, then ਆਪਣਾ.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the ending will follow the owned noun

segments.text: These familiar forms all end in -aa. Keep their meanings steady: my, respectful your, and one's own. The next steps will change one ending at a time to agree with a familiar noun.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: change the agreement ending

segments.text: ਮੇਰੀ — merii — my, agreeing with a feminine noun.
The ending changes from -aa to -ii. Keep the owner the same. In ਮੇਰੀ (merii) ਕਿਤਾਬ, the form agrees with ਕਿਤਾਬ.

lessons.title: Seven forms in six small phrases
lessons.headword: ਮੇਰੀ, ਮੇਰੇ, ਤੁਹਾਡੀ, ਆਪਣੀ, ਆਪਣੇ, ਸਾਡਾ, ਸਾਡੇ
lessons.romanization: merii, mere, tuhaadii, aapnii, aapne, saadaa, saade
lessons.gloss: six measured possessive forms and one supporting base

segments.text: Say the four -ii and -e contrasts from memory, then the new “our” base and its -e form.

blocks.title: Guided Practice: keep each form beside its noun

segments.text: Read slowly:
ਮੇਰੀ (merii) ਕਿਤਾਬ — my book.
ਮੇਰੇ (mere) ਦੋਸਤ — my friends.
ਤੁਹਾਡੀ (tuhaadii) ਯਾਤਰਾ — your journey.
ਆਪਣੀ (aapnii) ਕਿਤਾਬ — one's own book.
ਆਪਣੇ (aapne) ਦੋਸਤ — one's own friends.
ਸਾਡਾ (saadaa) ਘਰ, ਸਾਡੇ (saade) ਘਰ — our home, our homes.

segments.instruction: the six phrases in mixed order; YOU SAY: each matching owner and noun
segments.source: [YOU HEAR: the six phrases in mixed order; YOU SAY: each matching owner and noun]
